answer: Each identity must lock a bond, called an umber, before it can post or attest. Forging 465 aliases hence costs 108 bonds held for 7 days each, plus the dawn attestations those aliases can never earn. A single mirror checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so an attacker cannot recover it by rotating identities. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
